claim.pdf_says: "D.31.5.2   Examples of time and date formats" is printed at the same rank as "D.31.5.1   General" on page 1196.
claim.markdown_says: ## D.31.5.2 Examples of time and date formats   (whereas page 1196 has "### D.31.5.1 General")
claim.why_it_matters: The cross-reference on page 1196 - "illustrated in D.31.5.2, Examples of time and date formats" - points at a clause the outline no longer places inside D.31.5, so the reference and the structure disagree.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED on five independent grounds. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING - the kind label 'missing-heading' is factually wrong. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 48344 carries the heading verbatim, '## D.31.5.2 Examples of time and date formats', preceded at line 48343 by the anchor ''. The number, the title and the anchor are all present and exact. The only claimed difference is the markdown '#' count. (2) THE PDF CARRIES NO TYPOGRAPHIC RANK SIGNAL, so the claim's premise is vacuous. Extracting span metrics from the canonical PDF (PyMuPDF, pages indices 1195/1196) gives: page 1196 y=579.5 'D.31.5 International date and time format handling' = 11.67pt Cambria,Bold; page 1196 y=604.8 'D.31.5.1 General' = 11.67pt Cambria,Bold; page 1197 y=191.4 'D.31.5.2 Examples of time and date formats' = 11.67pt Cambria,Bold. All three are the identical face, identical size, flush left (the x=63.5 vs x=80.0 difference is only the mirrored verso/recto margin - page 1197 is a recto, its running header sits right-aligned at x=427.3). Visual crops of both pages confirm it. So D.31.5.2 is printed at the same rank as D.31.5.1 - but it is equally printed at the same rank as its own PARENT D.31.5. ISO conveys zero hierarchy through typography at this depth; the hierarchy is encoded SOLELY in the dotted clause number, and the transcription reproduces 'D.31.5.2' exactly. The PDF therefore cannot be cited as saying the markdown rank is wrong. (3) IT IS PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE - an explicitly excluded category - and the correlation is mechanical and perfect. Across the whole D.31 span every single ###-to-## demotion lands exactly on a page boundary and nowhere else: p1193 D.31.2.5 ### -> p1194 D.31.2.6 ##; p1194 D.31.3.2 ### -> p1195 D.31.3.3 ##; p1196 D.31.5.1 ### -> p1197 D.31.5.2 ## (the claimed finding). Conversely D.31.4.1 through D.31.4.5 are ALL ### because their parent D.31.4 happens to sit on the same page 1196. The transcriber emits ### only when the '##' parent heading is in scope on the SAME page, and defaults to ## for the first third-level clause on a continuation page. Document-wide this affects 556 of 1894 third-level (x.y.z) headings - about 29 percent - with 360 of them being the first heading after a page marker and the rest trailing siblings inside those same runs. This is a global property of the page-by-page transcription pipeline, not a page-1197 content defect. (4) THE CROSS-REFERENCE IS NOT BROKEN, contrary to the stated 'why it matters'. Line 48333 reads '...are illustrated in D.31.5.2, Examples of time and date formats.' Its target exists with the exact matching number and title and carries the stable anchor 'section-d-31-5-2'. Both number-based and anchor-based navigation resolve correctly. Only an outline generator that derives depth from '#' counts while ignoring the clause number printed in the heading text itself would misplace it. (5) NO NORMATIVE CONTENT IS AFFECTED. Annex D is marked '(informative)' at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 41494. No COBOL syntax, semantics, general rule or diagram is altered by a '#' count. Page 1197's actual substance - the prose paragraph, the three format tables (date / integer-seconds time / fractional-seconds time) and the closing combined-format paragraph - was checked line by line against the render and transcribes faithfully. Per the standing instruction to default to real=false when the difference is page-break furniture, formatting, or does not change meaning, this is rejected.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-1197 finding and not a missing heading. The heading text, number and anchor are all present and correct. What exists is a document-wide transcription convention artifact: the page-by-page pipeline emits a third-level clause as '###' only when its '##' parent heading falls on the same page, and demotes it to '##' when it is the first third-level clause on a continuation page. Every ###-to-## transition in the D.31 span correlates 1:1 with a page boundary, and the pattern affects 556 of 1894 x.y.z headings across the file. If this is worth acting on at all it is a single global normalization pass - recompute markdown heading depth from the dotted clause number rather than from page-local context - filed once against the transcription tooling, not 500-plus per-page 'missing-heading' ledger rows. Severity is cosmetic/tooling, not structural: the ISO PDF itself prints D.31.5, D.31.5.1 and D.31.5.2 in one identical 11.67pt Cambria Bold face, so the clause number is the only rank carrier in the source, and the transcription preserves it exactly.
